claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'EVALUATE statement, VI-84' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Conditional expression, VI-54'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'EVALUATE statement, VI-84' then '  Conditional expression, VI-54'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use '- ' list items). Entries and references match the PDF; informative content.

verdict.reasoning: I checked the printed page B-54 (PDF p966) at 300 dpi against page-966.md. The markdown holds every index entry and page reference in the printed order, one entry per line, with sub-entries indented two spaces under their main entry. That matches the printed layout: for example 'EVALUATE statement, VI-84' is followed by the indented 'Conditional expression, VI-54', and 'EXIT PROGRAM statement, X-33' by its three indented sub-entries. The claim itself concedes that the entries and references match. Its only complaint is how a Markdown renderer would lay the page out (no '- ' list markers, so the lines could merge into one paragraph) and that pages 961-962 use a different style. That is a formatting issue: the transcription's text and hierarchy are intact in the source, and no content differs from the PDF. The only other difference is a blank line at the column break before FILE-CONTROL, which is also formatting. The claim is rejected as formatting-only.
